meta.title: Shifts and dates
meta.description: How a day is cut into shifts — a regular length or a named pattern — and how many of them are rendered around the one being read.

basics.intro: A schedule is read one shift at a time, so the first thing the component does with your items is decide which shift each of them falls in. Regular shifts need two numbers: how long a shift is, and the wall-clock time one of them starts at. The rest of the day follows — six-hour shifts anchored at 06:00 start at 06:00, 12:00, 18:00 and 00:00.
basics.day: date picks the moment being read, and the shift containing that moment is the current one. A day is not a calendar day here: a night shift that runs from 22:00 to 06:00 is one shift, not two halves, and the grid and the list both treat it as one.

patterns.intro: When shifts are not all the same length, give a pattern instead: the start times, in order, each with a key of its own. An entry ends where the next one starts, and the last one wraps around midnight into the first. durationHours, anchor and keys are ignored when a pattern is given.

howMany.intro: before and after say how much of the surrounding day is rendered. They are the range a reader can scroll through and navigate within without your application fetching anything: outside it, moving on is a date change, which you handle.

points: Each shift is a section with a real heading, so a screen reader can jump between shifts by heading.
A shift heading says what the shift is relative to now — previous, current, next, or how many shifts away — and then its range, formatted in the reader's locale.
The range in the heading is text, not an image or a title attribute, so it is read and it is searchable.
Shifts outside the current one are not hidden from assistive technology: they are the same sections, in the same order as the visual grid.
formatters.shiftRange formats the range in a heading, formatters.hourLabel the hour labels of the timeline.
localization.shiftHeader holds the words for previous, current, next, earlier and later.
The shiftHeader, shiftHeaderTitle and shiftHeaderRange parts can be replaced through slots.
renderShiftHeader replaces the whole heading with your own, keeping the section around it.
durationHours has to divide 24, so shifts of five or seven hours are a pattern, not a regular length.
One pattern covers every day. A pattern that differs from weekday to weekend is not expressible yet; changing shifts with the date is the workaround.
Shifts are placed by timestamp in the reader's own time zone. A schedule read in two time zones shows two different cuts of the same items.
There is no way to hide a shift that has no items; an empty shift renders its empty state.
